title: "Carry and Roll-Down — Where a Bond's Return Comes From"

## A real question to answer

**If the market yield curve does not move, can a bond still generate a return before maturity?**

Yes. Time passes, you may receive coupons, and the bond becomes shorter. **Carry** and **roll-down** describe parts of this time-dependent return, but you must say exactly what 'unchanged curve' means.

## Build the exact relationship

$$
HPR=\frac{C+P_1-P_0}{P_0}
$$

**What every symbol means:** HPR is the return over the holding period; C is coupon cash received; P_0 is the starting bond price; P_1 is the end-of-period ex-coupon sale price, all in the same currency units.

**Substitute numbers and calculate:** Use our 5% annual two-year bond under a FLAT 5% curve. Buy at P_0=100. After one year receive C=5. Its remaining one-year payoff of 105 has ex-coupon value P_1=105/1.05=100, if the one-year yield stays 5%. HPR=(5+100−100)/100=5%.

## Why the financial reasoning works

With a sloping curve, a bond's new shorter maturity may lie at a different curve point even if the quoted maturity curve is held fixed. Its repriced value can change through **roll-down**, independently of coupons. In professional attribution models, carry, roll, curve-shape change and spread change have carefully specified conventions.

## A tiny calculation, not a large framework

~~~python
p0=100; coupon=5; p1=105/1.05
print((coupon+p1-p0)/p0) # 0.05
~~~

The examples are checked, where applicable, in the [small finance calculation lab](../examples/index.qmd).

## When this answer is no longer enough

An 'unchanged yield curve' scenario is different from forwards being realised as implied. It is a scenario, not a forecast. Real profits also depend on financing, accrued interest, transaction costs, reinvestment and credit spreads.

**Textbook basis:** Fabozzi Handbook 8e Ch. 6 (total return) and Part 10 (performance evaluation and return attribution).. The calculations and child-friendly explanations are original.
